name: luma.gl
category: A9. Adjacent resources mentioned during discovery
role: WebGL2/WebGPU engine under deck.gl; thin shader-and-pipeline layer
summary: vis.gl's GPU abstraction over WebGL2 and WebGPU: devices, buffers, shader modules, render pipelines and a small model/animation-loop layer. Driven from JavaScript in a browser page; output is canvas pixels captured by the harness. Its distinguishing role is being the renderer beneath deck.gl, not a scene-graph engine.
use_when: You need deck.gl internals or custom deck.gl layers with direct pipeline access
Writing raw WebGPU/WebGL2 pipelines with a shared abstraction over both backends
avoid_when: General 3D scenes: Three.js has loaders, materials and the ecosystem
Small shader work: regl or TWGL are lighter and simpler
Fullscreen-shader sketches: GLSLCanvas or OGL need less setup

assessment.rationale: Active, but duplicates catalogued low-level GPU layers (regl, twgl, ogl) and Three.js; its main value is as deck.gl's engine, which deck-gl already covers. No agent-facing route beyond a browser page.

notes: 2026-10-26: no headless capture test attempted; docs read only.
